title: tools
text:
A model can only write text. To read a file or run a command it calls a tool: a Python function whose name, docstring and typed parameters the backend turns into a schema the model sees. Ramabana’s tools come from shalya.
The tools act through a host. A host is the object that decides which folders are open (its roots), whether files may be written, and which other services exist, such as a shell, a Python kernel, git or the web. Each such service is a capability group. A host declares a group by inheriting the class that names it, such as CodeHost or WebHost, and Host.provides lists the groups it declares. Every host has the file group. The tools that need one capability group form a tool group: the shell group, for example, is run_shell, run_shell_bg, shell_output and shell_stop.
Shalya holds the host classes, the functions that build each tool group, the conventions tool results follow (err writes a failure that failed recognises), and the skills registry. This module re-exports all of them, so code that imports them from ramabana.tools keeps working, and Leela’s sys.modules[__name__] = ramabana.tools alias keeps resolving. New code imports them from shalya.
What this module adds needs parts of the agent that a toolset should not know about. A sub-agent needs a Backend to talk to and a Run to record it, and draws_itself needs a ModelSpec. The sections below cover a host that refuses everything, the image tools, tools_for, which builds the tool list a turn gets, delegation to sub-agents, and attachments.
source

getattr
def __getattr__(
    name
):
Resolve the deprecated Shalya compatibility surface without mirroring it here.
The re-exported names are shalya’s own objects, not copies. A copy could drift into a second implementation, so the cell below checks that every name in _all_ resolves and is the very object shalya holds. Shalya’s own notebooks test what the objects do.
len(_all_), sorted(_all_)[:8]
import shalya.core, shalya.host, shalya.skills, shalya.tools
here = sys.modules[__name__] if False else __import__('ramabana.tools', fromlist=['x'])
missing, different = [], []
for n in _all_:
    if not hasattr(here, n): missing.append(n); continue
    src = next((m for m in (shalya.core, shalya.host, shalya.skills, shalya.tools) if hasattr(m, n.lstrip('_')) or hasattr(m, n)), None)
    if src is None: continue
    theirs = getattr(src, n, None) or getattr(src, n.lstrip('_'), None)
    if getattr(here, n) is not theirs: different.append(n)
test_eq(missing, [])
test_eq(different, [])
test_eq((_cmds, _edits, _apply_edits, _diff),
        (shalya.core.cmds, shalya.core.edits, shalya.core.apply_edits, shalya.core.diff_text))
WRITE_TOOLS names every tool with an effect: tools that change files, the repository, the kernel, the shell, the vault or a browser page. It is the one name here that differs from shalya’s. The cart tools of the shop, cart_add and cart_remove, spend money, but they come from an extension rather than a host group, so shalya cannot know them and Ramabana adds them by name.
sorted(WRITE_TOOLS - shalya.core.WRITE_TOOLS)
test_eq(WRITE_TOOLS - shalya.core.WRITE_TOOLS, {'cart_add', 'cart_remove'})
assert shalya.core.WRITE_TOOLS < WRITE_TOOLS, 'nothing shalya marks may be dropped here'
The examples below run against a real LocalHost, the host the terminal uses, over a small project in a temporary folder. index=False skips building the semantic code index. provides lists the capability groups the host declares.
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'proj'
(root/'pkg').mkdir(parents=True)
(root/'pkg'/'sizes.py').write_text('def threshold(n):\n    "Half of n."\n    return n // 2\n')
local = LocalHost([root], index=False)
sorted(local.provides)
test_eq(sorted(local.provides), ['code', 'file', 'git', 'notebook', 'session', 'shell', 'web'])
test_eq(local.can('file'), True)

section: A host with nothing behind it
text:
A host with nothing behind it
NullHost is a host with no folders and no services. Checking a path raises HostError, reading returns nothing, and writing or deleting raises. It declares no capability group beyond file, and because its writes is False, tools_for gives it view_file and nothing else. Use it in a test, or wherever code needs a host object that must not touch the disk. The examples under it, and two further down, show each refusal.
The same cell adds delete and exists to LocalHost.


source

LocalHost.exists
def exists(
    path
):
Whether path is a file inside the roots (an undecodable file counts).




source

LocalHost.delete
def delete(
    path
):
Remove one file inside the roots; one already gone is not an error.




source

NullHost
def NullHost(
    roots:tuple=()
):
A host with no folders and no services, which refuses every file operation.



test_eq([t.__name__ for t in tools_for(NullHost())], ['view_file'])
test_eq(NullHost().writes, False)
test_fail(lambda: NullHost().write('/a', 'x'), contains='cannot write')

title: tools
text:
Drawing
Shalya’s generate_image tool makes pictures. Some models can draw themselves when they are given the image tool. For any other model the prompt goes to a separate image model. Which case applies is a fact about the turn’s model, so shalya asks for it as a callable, and this module supplies the callable.
draws_itself looks up a model’s capabilities with spec_caps and returns True when image is among the tools the model supports (Caps.tools). The supported_output_modalities field cannot answer this: it says no for every chat model, because it describes what a model returns without being asked.


source

image_tools
def image_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000, session:str='', get_spec:NoneType=None, on_media:NoneType=None
):
Shalya’s image tools for host, checking the turn’s model on every call.




source

draws_itself
def draws_itself(
    spec
):
Whether the model behind spec can draw pictures itself when given the image tool.


The example fakes the capability table with mock_caps, so it runs without a model. The first spec lists image among its tools and the second does not. No spec at all gives False.

from types import SimpleNamespace
draws = ModelSpec('drawer', 'remote', 'openai/gpt-5.6-luna')
plain = ModelSpec('plain', 'remote', 'openai/gpt-5.6')
caps = {'openai/gpt-5.6-luna': SimpleNamespace(tools=('image', 'search')), 'openai/gpt-5.6': SimpleNamespace(tools=('search',))}
with mock_caps(caps): got = draws_itself(draws), draws_itself(plain), draws_itself(None)
got

(True, False, False)



with mock_caps(caps):
    test_eq(draws_itself(draws), True)
    test_eq(draws_itself(plain), False)
test_eq(draws_itself(None), False)
with mock_caps({}): test_eq(draws_itself(draws), False)

image_tools builds shalya’s image group for a host, with draws_itself asked about the turn’s model each time the tool is called. Pass get_spec, a callable returning the current ModelSpec, so that a model switch mid-session is seen. Without an image API key the tool returns a message saying so and makes no request, which is why this example runs anywhere.

gen = image_tools(local, get_spec=lambda: draws)[0]
gen.__name__, image_available()


test_eq(gen.__name__, 'generate_image')
if not image_available(): assert 'OPENAI_API_KEY' in gen('a kettle')
assert failed(gen('a kettle', size='3x3'))
test_eq(len(image_tools(local, get_spec=lambda: None)), 1)

title: tools
text:
Assembling the tool list
tools_for decides which tools a host gets. It asks Host.provides for the capability groups and adds the tool group for each. A get_skills callable adds read_skill, and extra adds extension tools. drop removes groups by name, such as 'shell' or 'image'. optin adds groups that are off by default: exhash (the hash-addressed edit_file), research, author, legacy (tool names from older releases) and browser.
Shalya has a tools_for of its own. Use this one in Ramabana code, because it also builds the image group from the turn’s model through get_spec and on_media, which a host cannot know. The image group comes only when an image key is set and the host can write, since generate_image saves files. On a LocalHost without litesearch installed, search_code is left out.
small_tool marks an extension tool to keep in the small profile, the short catalog a local model or a small context window gets. ToolCatalog wraps a tool list once and answers questions about it: each tool’s group, which tools write, which have effects, and a read-only copy. ToolEntry is one row of it.


source

ToolCatalog
def ToolCatalog(
    tools:tuple=()
):
An immutable list of tools that answers each one’s group, whether it writes, and whether it has effects.




source

ToolEntry
def ToolEntry(
    tool:object, group:str=''
)->None:
One callable and the Shalya metadata every consumer needs.

small_tool
def small_tool(
    f
):
Mark an extension tool for the small profile, whose catalog omits unmarked tools.




source

tools_for
def tools_for(
    host, get_skills:NoneType=None, extra:tuple=(), mx:int=6000, drop:tuple=(), get_spec:NoneType=None,
    on_media:NoneType=None, optin:tuple=()
):
The tools for host: a group per capability it declares, plus skills, images and extensions, less drop and plus optin.


The list for the real host above. It has the file, code, notebook, shell, git and web groups. The memory and API tools are absent because LocalHost does not declare those groups here, and generate_image appears only when an image key is set.

sorted(t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local))


ts = tools_for(local)
names = {t.__name__ for t in ts}
assert {'search_code', 'view_file', 'run_python', 'run_shell'} <= names, sorted(names)
assert not (names & {'memory_tree', 'api_load', 'ask_memory'})
test_eq('generate_image' in names, image_available())
test_eq(names - {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local, drop=['shell'])},
        {'run_shell', 'run_shell_bg', 'shell_output', 'shell_stop'})
assert 'read_skill' in {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local, get_skills=lambda: [])}
assert 'read_skill' not in names
_installed, installed = installed, lambda m: m != 'litesearch'
try: assert 'search_code' not in {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local)}
finally: installed = _installed

Opt-in groups come only on request. edit_file appears with optin=('exhash',), the old tool names with optin='legacy', and an unknown name raises.

assert 'edit_file' not in names
assert 'edit_file' in {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local, optin=('exhash',))}
assert 'list_files' in {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(local, optin='legacy')}
test_fail(lambda: tools_for(local, optin=('nosuch',)), contains='unknown optin')


h = NullHost(['/proj'])
sorted(h.provides), [t.__name__ for t in tools_for(h)]


test_eq(sorted(h.provides), ['file'])
test_eq(h.roots, ['/proj'])
test_fail(lambda: h.check('a.py'), contains='no folders are open')

Every method of NullHost refuses. Checking a path raises because no folders are open, reading gives nothing, and opening another folder raises. It is the reference for how a host says “I cannot”.

h.walk(), h.read('a.py'), h.text_at('a.py')


test_eq(h.walk(), [])
test_eq(h.read('a.py'), None)
test_eq(h.text_at('a.py'), None)
test_fail(lambda: h.write('a.py', 'x'), contains='cannot write')
test_fail(lambda: h.check('a.py'), contains='no folders are open')
test_fail(lambda: NullHost().add_root('/tmp'), contains='cannot open another folder')

title: tools
text:
Sub-agents
A sub-agent is a separate conversation with a model, started to answer one question for the agent that asked. Handing a question over this way is delegation. Its purpose is to save context, not time. A broad question can take twenty tool calls to answer, and if the main agent made them itself every result would stay in its conversation. Delegated, the same work costs the main conversation one question and one answer, because the sub-agent’s conversation is thrown away when it finishes.
A sub-agent gets read-only tools unless the session allows it to write. NO_SUB lists the tools it never gets by default: the four delegation tools and the folder watches, which would outlive its task. A session that allows nesting passes its own block, and then the sub-agent may delegate in turn. SUB_MAX_STEPS, SUB_TIMEOUT and SUB_SLOTS are the default step limit, the default time limit, and how many sub-agents may work at once.
A briefing is the standing instructions a model gets before the conversation starts, its system prompt. sub_briefing builds a sub-agent’s from parts: SUB_SP_HEAD, which every sub-agent gets, then SUB_READ_SP or SUB_WRITE_SP, then an optional note on how much of the answer the caller will read, then notes for the model’s family.


source

sub_briefing
def sub_briefing(
    writes:bool=False, answer_max:int=0, # characters the caller reads of the answer; 0 says nothing about it
    notes:str='', # the sub-agent model's family notes, after the rest
):
The sub-agent standing instructions: the shared half, the read-only or the write half, the answer budget and the family notes.




source

inbox_note
def inbox_note(
    key
):
The one tag the model may take as the user: it carries key, which no file or page knows.


SUB_SP is the read-only briefing with nothing added, and it is the default. A sub-agent allowed to write gets SUB_SP_HEAD followed by SUB_WRITE_SP.

SUB_MAX_STEPS, len(SUB_SP.split()), len(SUB_WRITE_SP.split())


assert 'State plainly when you find nothing' in SUB_SP
assert 'cannot edit' in SUB_SP
assert SUB_MAX_STEPS > 0
test_eq(sorted(NO_SUB), ['cancel_watch', 'delegate_async', 'delegate_cancel', 'delegate_result', 'delegate_search', 'watch'])

read_only, from shalya, filters a tool list down to what an agent may have when it must not change anything. Write tools are dropped, or swapped for a safe version where the tool has one. block drops tools by name, and Ramabana passes NO_SUB. effects=False also drops the acting tools, those that do something without writing a file, such as inspect_python, shell_stop and generate_image. Shalya marks them with acts and lists them in ACTING_TOOLS. Use effects=False for a surface that may look and propose but never act.
A safe version can fix an argument. In the second cell below, read_url still fetches the page, but its remember parameter is gone and it no longer stores the page in the vault.

[t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts, block=NO_SUB)]


import inspect


test_eq(set(t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts, block=NO_SUB)) & WRITE_TOOLS, set())
shut = set(t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts, effects=False, block=NO_SUB))
test_eq(shut & (WRITE_TOOLS | NO_SUB | ACTING_TOOLS), set())
test_eq('search_code' in shut, True)

kept = []
class Page: text = 'page'
class Keeps(MemHost, WebHost):
    def web_search(self, query, n=20): return []
    def research(self, query): return ''
    def read_url(self, url, remember=True): kept.append(remember); return Page()
fetch = next(t for t in read_only(tools_for(Keeps({'/proj/a.py': 'x = 1\n'}))) if t.__name__ == 'read_url')
fetch(url='https://example.com')
test_eq(kept, [False])
test_eq('remember' in inspect.signature(fetch).parameters, False)
sorted(set(t.__name__ for t in ts) & ACTING_TOOLS)

max_calls puts a hard budget on the list. Past it, every tool returns a message telling the model to stop and answer. Local engines run their own tool loop, so Ramabana cannot stop them between steps, and a budget inside the tools is the one limit that works on every backend. Below, the second search is refused.

budgeted = read_only(ts, max_calls=1, block=NO_SUB)
search = next(t for t in budgeted if t.__name__ == 'search_code')
search('return'), search('return')

delegate asks one question of a sub-agent. It spawns a new conversation on the same engine as backend, hands it the tools that read_only lets through (all of them with writes=True), sends the question, and closes the conversation in a finally block whether or not it succeeded. It returns the answer text. An empty or repetitive answer is replaced by a notice that the delegation failed, and a sub-agent that raised gives an error result. timeout cancels the run after that many seconds, and slots, a shared Slots, makes it wait for a free place among the sub-agents working at once. A sub-agent waiting on sub-agents of its own lends its place back, so a full tree of delegations cannot deadlock.
Use delegate for one question. delegate_many, below, asks several, and subagent_tools wraps both as tools a model can call.


source

delegate
def delegate(
    backend, question, tools:tuple=(), sp:NoneType=None, max_steps:int=60, skills:tuple=(),
    writes:bool=False, # hand over WRITE_TOOLS as well
    approve:NoneType=None, # the gate those writes answer to
    run:NoneType=None, # a pre-registered child run
    images:tuple=(), # picture bytes sent with the question
    block:frozenset=frozenset({'cancel_watch', 'delegate_async', 'watch', 'delegate_result', 'delegate_search', 'delegate_cancel'}), # tool names withheld from the sub-agent
    timeout:int=0, # seconds before the run is cancelled; 0 never
    slots:NoneType=None, # a shared `Slots`, held while the sub-agent works
):
Ask question of a sub-agent in a separate conversation on backend’s engine, and return its answer text.

A bound on sub-agents working at once; one waiting on its own sub-agents lends its slot back.

sub_sp
def sub_sp(
    sp:str="You are a research sub-agent in a Python IDE. Answer the delegated question only.\n- Use tools as needed. Report findings with file paths and line numbers.\n- Before each tool call, write one line of at most eight words, in the -ing form, saying what you are doing.\n- State plainly when you find nothing. Do not guess.\n- A claim that something ran, exists or failed names the tool call or artifact behind it. Anything else is a hypothesis; say so.\n- End with one line: `state: completed`, `state: blocked` or `state: failed`, and why.\n- A tool result saying the tool-call budget is spent, and the request to answer that follows it, come from this harness: answer then with what you found.\n- You cannot edit. Describe any required change and stop.\n- Use `inspect_python` for live variables. Its default scope is sandboxed; use `scope='overlay'` for the real interpreter.",
    skills:tuple=()
):
A sub-agent’s briefing: standing instructions, then the bodies of skills its task named.


The tools a sub-agent gets are wrapped. A message sent to a running sub-agent, with /tell in the terminal, arrives appended to its next tool result inside a <user-message> tag that carries the run’s key. inbox_note tells the sub-agent that only a tag with that key is the user speaking, since a file or a web page could contain the same tag. A sub-agent that gets the same result from the same call REPEAT_CALLS times in a row is told to change course. The cell below shows a queued message arriving with a result.

r = Run('run_t'); r.tell('and the tests')
test_eq(_inboxed(lambda: 'contents', lambda: None)(), 'contents')
test_eq(_inboxed(lambda: 'contents', lambda: r)(), f'contents\n\n<user-message key="{r.key}">\nand the tests\n</user-message>')
test_eq(r.drain_inbox(), [])

Each wrapped call also marks the run as active, so the now pane, the side panel that lists live runs (see pane), can show what a sub-agent is doing. Some backends, LiteRT for one, never pass on the text a model writes between calls. Their sub-agents get a status tool from status_tool to report one line instead, and STATUS_NOTE in the briefing tells them to use it.

class _Quiet(FakeBackend):
    narrates = False
    def spawn(self, sp='', tools=(), **kw):
        self.sub = FakeBackend(self.spec, sp=sp, tools=tools, shared=True)
        self.sub._send = lambda msg, **kw: next(t for t in self.sub.tools if t.__name__ == 'status')(text='Reading the tests')
        return self.sub

qb, qr = _Quiet(), Run('run_quiet', 'child', 'q')
delegate(qb, 'q', tools=ts, run=qr)
test_eq(qr.status, 'Reading the tests')
assert STATUS_NOTE in qb.sub.sp



source

delegate_many
def delegate_many(
    backend, questions, tools:tuple=(), sp:NoneType=None, max_steps:int=60, n_workers:int=4, skills:tuple=(),
    writes:bool=False, approve:NoneType=None, parent:NoneType=None, images:tuple=(),
    block:frozenset=frozenset({'cancel_watch', 'delegate_async', 'watch', 'delegate_result', 'delegate_search', 'delegate_cancel'}),
    timeout:int=0, slots:NoneType=None
):
Ask several questions of one sub-agent each, and return the answers in question order.


Here a fake backend answers a delegated question. The caller gets back only the answer text.

be = FakeBackend(replies=['the caller never sees this'])
delegate(be, 'which files import fastllm?', tools=ts)

The spawned conversation was separate. It held only the question and the answer, and delegate closed it before returning.

test_eq(len(be.spawned), 1)
be.spawned[0].hist

delegate_many asks several questions at once, one sub-agent each, and returns the answers in the order the questions were asked. It registers every child run with the parent before any starts, so cancelling the parent reaches all of them; the last example on this page shows that. It runs the questions one at a time when sub-agents may write, and when the model is local, because an engine such as LiteRT holds one conversation at a time and parallel runs would race for it.

delegate_many(be, ['what imports fastllm?', 'where is compaction triggered?'], tools=ts)

The delegation tools take callables that return a backend, not a backend. Each call asks for the current session’s backend, so after a /model switch the next sub-agent runs on the new model.
delegate_async starts a sub-agent in the background and returns at once, so the turn can carry on while it works. Background keeps track of those runs. start registers a run before its thread begins, so a status call always finds the id it returned. At most mx runs reach a model at once (ASYNC_MAX, 4 by default) and the rest wait as pending. status, result and cancel answer for one run, and status with no id answers for all. The last keep answers are held. close, called when the session ends, cancels every run and refuses new work.
The examples hold two runs behind a register with one place, cancel a run still waiting, close a register, catch a run that raised, and show an answer dropped once newer ones push it out.


source

Background
def Background(
    mx:int=4, # how many reach a model at once
    keep:int=50, # answers held before the oldest is dropped
    on_done:NoneType=None, # called with `(run, answer)` when a run finishes
):
Delegations running behind the turn that asked for them, and the answers they leave.



bg = Background(mx=1)
gate, seen = threading.Event(), []

def slow(run):
    run.start()
    seen.append(run.id)
    gate.wait(5)
    return f'answered {run.question}'

a = bg.start(slow, Run('run_a', 'child', 'first'))
b = bg.start(slow, Run('run_b', 'child', 'second'))
time.sleep(.2)
[(r['id'], r['state']) for r in bg.status()]


test_eq({r['id'] for r in bg.status()}, {'run_a', 'run_b'})
test_eq(bg.status('run_a')[0]['state'], 'running')
test_eq(bg.status('run_b')[0]['state'], 'pending')
test_eq(len(seen), 1)

assert 'is running' in bg.result('run_a')
assert bg.result('nope').startswith('no delegation named')
assert bg.status('nope').startswith('no delegation named')

gate.set()
for _ in range(200):
    if bg.result('run_b').startswith('answered'): break
    time.sleep(.02)
test_eq(bg.result('run_a'), 'answered first')
test_eq(bg.result('run_b'), 'answered second')
test_eq(len(seen), 2)


held = Background(mx=1)
block, ran = threading.Event(), []
held.start(lambda r: (r.start(), block.wait(5), ran.append(r.id))[2], Run('run_1', 'child', 'holds the slot'))
held.start(lambda r: ran.append(r.id), Run('run_2', 'child', 'never runs'))
time.sleep(.2)
test_eq(held.cancel('run_2'), 'run_2 is stopping')
block.set()
for _ in range(200):
    if 'stopped' in held.result('run_2'): break
    time.sleep(.02)
assert 'stopped (cancelled)' in held.result('run_2'), held.result('run_2')
test_eq(ran, ['run_1'])
assert held.cancel('run_2').startswith('run_2 had already finished')


shut = Background()
shut.start(lambda r: 'done', Run('run_x', 'child', 'q'))
test_eq(shut.close(), 1)
test_fail(lambda: shut.start(lambda r: 'nope', Run('run_y', 'child', 'q')),
          contains='while the session is closing')
test_eq(shut.status('run_y'), "no delegation named 'run_y' was started here")

boom = Background()
boom.start(lambda r: 1/0, Run('run_z', 'child', 'q'))
for _ in range(200):
    if ERR in boom.result('run_z'): break
    time.sleep(.02)
assert 'ZeroDivisionError' in boom.result('run_z'), boom.result('run_z')

small = Background(keep=1)
for n in ('run_p', 'run_q'): small.start(lambda r: f'ans {r.id}', Run(n, 'child', 'q'))
for _ in range(200):
    if small.result('run_q') == 'ans run_q': break
    time.sleep(.02)
assert 'no longer held' in small.result('run_p'), small.result('run_p')



source

subagent_tools
def subagent_tools(
    get_backend, get_tools, get_skills:NoneType=None, get_cloud_backend:NoneType=None,
    get_writes:NoneType=None, # the session's sub-agent write toggle, read per call
    get_approve:NoneType=None, # the gate those writes answer to
    background:NoneType=None, # async delegation register; made if None
    get_log_dir:NoneType=None, # callable -> the folder run transcripts go in, or None
    get_pictures:NoneType=None, # callable paths -> `(bytes, err)`; see `read_pictures`
    get_steps:NoneType=None, # callable -> the step budget, which also caps a call's `max_steps`
    get_timeout:NoneType=None, # callable -> seconds each delegation may run; 0 never stops it
    get_max:NoneType=None, # callable -> chars one result may spend, notes included; `MAX_TOOL_CHARS` when None

subagent_tools builds the four tools a model uses to delegate. delegate_search asks one or more questions and waits for the answers. delegate_async starts one question in the background and returns a run id. delegate_result collects a background answer, or with no id lists every background run, and delegate_cancel stops one. Every argument is a callable read on each call, so the backend, the step budget, the time limit and the write setting follow the session as they change. An answer longer than one tool result may be is cut, and the whole text is saved to a file whose path the cut answer names.

subs = {t.__name__: t for t in subagent_tools(lambda: be, lambda: ts)}
delegate_search = subs['delegate_search']
list(subs)

With no model to delegate to, the tools return a message saying so instead of raising into the turn. With a model, several questions come back with one heading each.

picture_mime recognises a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF by its first bytes, whatever the file is called, which is why fake.png holding text is refused below. The limits are the terminal’s: at most MAX_ATTACH pictures, each at most MAX_MEDIA bytes. Every question’s sub-agent receives every picture, so pictures times questions may not exceed MAX_ATTACH.
A read-only sub-agent’s generate_image refuses a path, because saving there would be a write, and saves under media/ instead. PATH_WRITES, path_write and write_targets tell the approval gate about this case: a call to a tool in PATH_WRITES counts as a write when it names a path, and write_targets lists the files any call will write.

    (pic_root/name).write_text(body); assert 'not a picture' in read_pictures(pic_host, [name])[1], name

with open(pic_root/'big.png', 'wb') as f: f.write(png); f.truncate(MAX_MEDIA + 1)
assert 'over' in read_pictures(pic_host, ['big.png'])[1]
too_many = pt['delegate_search'](['q%d' % i for i in range(MAX_ATTACH + 1)], images=['refs/rama.png'])
assert 'at most' in too_many, too_many

drawn = FakeBackend()
delegate(drawn, 'draw', tools=[generate_image])

assert failed(sub_draw('x', path='main.py')) and 'read-only' in sub_draw('x', path='main.py')

test_eq({t.__name__: t for t in drawn.spawned[-1].tools}['generate_image']('x', path='a.png'), 'drew a.png')

delegate_many registers every child run before any work starts. Cancelling the parent stops the child that is running, and the children still queued never spawn. The fake backend below blocks on its first question until it is cancelled.

class _Sub:
    max_steps = 0
    def __init__(self, owner): self.owner, self.release = owner, threading.Event()
    def send(self, question, run=None):
        self.owner.started.append(question); self.release.wait(); return 'late'
    def cancel(self): self.owner.cancelled += 1; self.release.set(); return True
    def close(self): pass

class _ParentBackend:
    def __init__(self):
        self.spec = AttrDict(name='fake-child', local=False)
        self.started, self.spawned, self.cancelled = [], 0, 0
    def spawn(self, **kw): self.spawned += 1; return _Sub(self)

backend, parent, box = _ParentBackend(), Run('run_parent', grace=.03), []
parent.start()
t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: box.extend(delegate_many(backend, ['a', 'b', 'c'], n_workers=1, parent=parent)), daemon=True)
t.start()
while not backend.started: time.sleep(.001)
test_eq(len(parent.children), 3)
parent.cancel(); t.join(.2)
test_eq((backend.spawned, backend.cancelled), (1, 1))
test_eq(len(box), 3)
assert all((isinstance(x, dict) and x['state'] in ('cancelled', 'detached'))
           or (isinstance(x, str) and 'cancelled' in x) for x in box)

text:
Two small fixes to teleprint are applied when this module loads. Each checks whether the installed teleprint already has the fix and does nothing if so; FRAME_PATCHED and INK_PATCHED record whether the patch was needed.
The first concerns rows already written to the scrollback. Teleprint keeps a mark, _ws, of how many rows of the document it has committed there, and each frame writes only the rows past the mark. Those rows are history in the terminal and cannot be taken back. When a tool result folds, the document gets shorter, and teleprint used to lower the mark to match, so the next frame wrote earlier rows a second time. A session with many folded calls ended up with many copies of its startup banner. The patch keeps the mark from ever going down.
The second adds a hook, Compositor.on_frame, which runs after each paint. Pictures need it: a picture is placed on the screen after the text is drawn, as the section on pictures below explains. The hook is installed before the mark fix, so _frame.__wrapped__ is the frame without the mark fix, and the test below uses it to show the duplicated rows.
from teleprint.testing import EmuTty as _EmuTty
async def _marks_over_a_fold(frame):
    "The ink mark after growth, after a fold, and after growing again, under `frame`."
    tty = _EmuTty(40, 8)
    comp = Compositor(tty); comp._register_signals = lambda: None
    await comp.start()
    comp.print_block(Text('BANNER'), tag='note', collapse_at=None, source='BANNER')
    tall = comp.print_block(Text('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(20))), tag='tool',
                            collapse_at=None, source='x')
    out = []
    frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    tall.collapsed, tall.collapse_at = True, 1
    comp._dirty(tall); frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    comp.print_block(Text('\n'.join(f'again {i}' for i in range(20))), tag='tool',
                     collapse_at=None, source='y')
    frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    tty.close()
    return out

_marks = await _marks_over_a_fold(Compositor._frame)
assert _marks[0] > 0, 'the document has to outgrow the window for anything to be inked at all'
test_eq(_marks, sorted(_marks))

if INK_PATCHED:
    _bare = await _marks_over_a_fold(Compositor._frame.__wrapped__)
    test_eq(_bare[1], 0)
    assert _bare != sorted(_bare)
_h_tty = _EmuTty(30, 6)
_h_comp = Compositor(_h_tty); _h_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await _h_comp.start()
_fired = []
_h_comp.on_frame = lambda: _fired.append(_h_comp._cursor)
_h_comp.print_block(Text('one'), tag='note')
test_eq(len(_fired), 1)
_h_comp.paused = True
_h_comp.print_block(Text('two'), tag='note')
test_eq(len(_fired), 1)
_h_tty.close()
Ramabana gives shift+enter its own meaning: during a turn it queues the line as the next turn, where plain enter steers the running one. By default a terminal sends the same byte for both keys, so the program has to ask the terminal for richer key reports. There are two protocols for this:
The compositor asks for both, and each terminal answers with the one it supports. ext_key turns either report into the same Key the old byte parser would have produced. Once kitty’s flag is on, esc, control letters and alt letters also arrive in the new form, so the decoder has to cover every key, and it follows these rules:
ext_keys_ok decides whether to ask at all: only when both stdin and stdout are a real terminal, so tests and pipes never see the escape codes. The compositor turns the modes off wherever it hands the terminal back: at stop, at release when another program borrows the terminal, before a fatal signal, and while ctrl+z has the process suspended. A ctrl+z from the transcript view also leaves the alternate screen while suspended and comes back on fg. Kitty keeps a separate flag stack for the alternate screen, so the transcript view sets the flag again there and clears it before leaving.

title: cli
text:
Blocks and keys
Every block has a kind, and each kind has its own gutter, the mark in the left margin. GUTTERS maps the nine kinds to their marks: user for your prompts (▌), step for the agent’s narration (┆), tool for a tool call (│), reply for the answer, ask for an approval question (◆), plan for the plan checklist (▸), note for a message from Ramabana itself (·), error (×), and media for a picture.
A turn is one prompt and everything the agent does to answer it. In the transcript it reads as a timeline in the order the work happened: a step for each stretch of narration, a tool block for each call that narration introduced, and one reply with the answer at the end. Results fold to one row and narration stays visible, so the answer always sits below the narration that led to it.
The cell below also holds the palettes. DARK, GRUVBOX and the other dicts name the colours of each theme, set_theme picks the active one, and code_theme, hl_theme and code_bg give the matching colours for highlighted code. plan_text draws the plan checklist in the active palette.

title: cli
text:
Attachments
A prompt can carry files with it: pictures, sound, or text. In the terminal you attach one in three ways. You can drop the file on the window, paste its path, or write @path in the prompt. All three end up as the same attachment. The path parser accepts quoted paths, paths in brackets, file:// URIs and backslash-escaped spaces, and a plain sentence that merely mentions a path is left alone, as the tests below check.
A picture goes to the model as an image content part, the form a model API takes images in. Every attachment also carries its absolute path, and the path still works when the model cannot take the content part. A model without audio support, for example, can still open a .wav through the file tools.
The attachment helpers themselves, media_paths, Attachment, media_parts and the rest, live in ramabana.tools and are imported here so the terminal and the other frontends share one parser.

Pictures, drawn where the terminal can draw
A picture can reach the screen in two ways. The model can return one in Resp.media, or a tool can write an image file during the turn and report it through on_media. On a terminal without kitty graphics, the picture is saved and its path printed. kitty_graphics decides which kind of terminal this is, from the environment variables and $TERM names in KITTY_ENV and KITTY_TERM.
On a terminal with kitty graphics the picture is drawn in place. Kitty positions an image by screen cell, separately from the text. The compositor redraws its document with absolute cursor moves, so an image cannot ride along in the text the way prose does. A Picture handles this in two steps. Picture.send transfers the image bytes to the terminal once. The block itself holds only the blank rows the picture will cover, sized by img_cells from png_size. Then Picture.place writes a short placement command at the end of every frame, at the current position of those blank rows. Each placement reuses the picture’s image id, which replaces the previous placement, so repaints never stack copies. If the terminal clears the cells under an image, the next frame places it again.
picture builds a Picture for a file, or returns None when this terminal or this file cannot be drawn. draw_png is for code that has no frames to hook into: it sends and places a picture at the cursor in one go. media_line is the transcript line for a saved picture.
Kitty also offers Unicode placeholders, where the image is anchored to special characters in the text. They are not used, because Kaku and at least one other terminal ignore the U=1 flag, draw at the cursor, and print U+10EEEE as a missing glyph, which leaves a block of boxes behind the picture.

import os as _osr, struct as _struct, zlib as _zlib

def _a_png(w, h):
    "A real noise PNG, big enough to need several APC chunks."
    def chunk(tag, data):
        return (_struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + tag + data
                + _struct.pack('>I', _zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xffffffff))
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + _osr.urandom(3 * w) for _ in range(h))
    return (b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', _struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))
            + chunk(b'IDAT', _zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))


import os as _os
_seen = {k: _os.environ.pop(k, None) for k in (*KITTY_ENV, 'TERM', 'TERM_PROGRAM')}
try:
    test_eq(kitty_graphics(), False)
    test_eq(picture('/tmp/nope.png'), None)
    test_eq(draw_png('/tmp/nope.png'), '')
    assert media_line('/tmp/a.png').startswith('saved  ')

    import tempfile
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        png = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + b'x'
        p = save_media({'mime': 'image/png', 'data': png}, d)
        test_eq(p.name, 'image-1.png')
        test_eq(p.read_bytes(), png)
        test_eq(p.parent.name, 'media')
        test_eq(save_media({'mime': 'image/png', 'data': png}, d).name, 'image-2.png')
        test_eq(save_media({'mime': 'image/avif', 'data': png}, d).suffix, '.avif')

    _os.environ['RAMABANA_KITTY'] = '1'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        p = Path(d)/'a.png'
        p.write_bytes(_a_png(1200, 600))
        pic = picture(p, 24)
        test_eq((pic.cols, pic.rows), (24, 6))
        assert len(pic.send()) > 2 * APC_CHUNK
        test_eq(pic.send().count('m=0'), 1)
        assert 'a=t' in pic.send() and 'a=p' not in pic.send()
        test_eq(pic.place(), f'\x1b_Ga=p,i={pic.id},p=1,c=24,r=6,C=1,q=2\x1b\\')
        test_eq(len(pic.gap().plain.split('\n')), 6)
        test_eq(pic.gap().plain.split('\n')[0], 'a.png')

title: cli
text:
The turn
A turn starts when you press enter on a prompt. run_turn runs one turn and streams it into the transcript. The agent’s agent.stream is a blocking generator that runs on a separate model thread, so run_turn reads its chunks from a queue. That keeps the event loop free to handle keystrokes, approval questions and activity updates while the model works.
Before the turn starts, some prompts get a row of choices. A request such as “refactor the runtime” can mean “make the change”, “propose a plan”, or “say what is in scope”, and learning which one the model picked is costly. options_for checks the typed line against the trigger words in MENUS and returns a title and a list of Options, or None. ChoiceMenu draws the row above the input line and handles the keys that move through it and pick one. Each Option carries the instruction it appends to the prompt (its suffix), so the choice reaches the model as part of what you asked for. The REFACTOR options are the only menu at present. The examples of the menu in use come later, under the surface.
close_done_shells closes the tmux panes of run_shell_bg commands that have finished; their output stays readable through cmd_output.

title: cli
text:
The surface
Ui is the whole terminal surface, and the class the rest of this page builds on. It has three jobs. It paints the tail, the status bar and input line at the bottom of the screen. It turns tool calls and approval requests into blocks. And it decides what each keystroke means: on_key returns a coroutine for the caller to start (a turn, for example), the string 'quit', or None when the key was handled.
Every method on Ui is synchronous and does no terminal I/O of its own, so the examples below drive it against an emulated terminal with no mocks. The one care it takes is with threads. Activity and approval callbacks arrive on the model’s worker thread, and only the event loop thread may touch the compositor, so those callbacks are handed to the loop through _post.
The class is long, and later cells add to it with fastcore’s @patch. The methods a caller is most likely to use are submit for the typed line, say to print a block, note for a one-line message, stream for reply text as it arrives, and paint to redraw.


source

Ui
def Ui(
    comp, agent, loop:NoneType=None
):
The terminal surface: a transcript of blocks, a status bar, and one line to type in.


A line starting with /name that is not one of the agent’s slash commands is looked up as a skill or a command file. Command files are markdown files in <cfg>/commands/*.md, plus a root’s .agents/commands/ once the project_extensions option is turned on. So /exhash fix the loop sends the prompt “fix the loop” with the exhash skill attached, instead of reporting an unknown command. In a command file, $ARGUMENTS is replaced by everything after the name, $1 to $n by its separate words, and each @path by that file when it lies inside the open folders. A command file with subtask: true in its frontmatter is sent as a task for delegate_async, which runs it in a sub-agent.
The approval keys come next. While an approval question waits, y approves, n refuses, and lowercase a approves this request and everything else for the rest of the session. Capital A approves and also adds a rule that always allows requests like this one, through always_allow, when the approval gate can hold rules; ask_pattern is what that rule matches. Without rules, A behaves like a. parse_answer reads a typed answer such as y, no or n: put it in docs/.
A waiting question rings the terminal bell with ring, but only once nobody has typed for BELL_IDLE seconds. nudge shows the question again every REASK_EVERY seconds while it waits, and reask does the showing. #note TEXT at the prompt calls note_memory, which keeps the line for the next session’s memory.

from types import SimpleNamespace

class _QueueWork:
    def __init__(self): self.closed = False
    def close(self): self.closed = True

class _QueueTask:
    def add_done_callback(self, callback): self.callback = callback
    def done(self): return False

class _QueueComp:
    def __init__(self): self.blocks, self.started = {}, None
    def remove_block(self, block): self.blocks.pop(block.id)
    def spawn(self, work, name):
        self.started = work
        return _QueueTask()

class _QueueUi:
    agent = SimpleNamespace(leftovers=lambda: [])
    _echo, _retract, _replay = Ui._echo, Ui._retract, Ui._replay
    _turn_over, start_turn, _next_queued, take_back = Ui._turn_over, Ui.start_turn, Ui._next_queued, Ui.take_back
    _queued_prompt = Ui._queued_prompt
    flash, mark_read = Ui.flash, Ui.mark_read
    def __init__(self, turn=None):
        self.comp, self.turn = _QueueComp(), turn
        self._queued, self._queued_echo, self._echoed = None, [], []
        self._steered, self._queued_typed = [], ''
        self._queued_text, self._typed, self._prompt, self._flash = [], '', None, None
        self.buf = SimpleNamespace(text='', cursor=0)
        self.notes, self.painted, self.attachments = [], False, []
    def say(self, body, kind='reply', **kw):
        block = type('Block', (), {'id': len(self.comp.blocks) + 1, 'body': str(body), 'tag': kind})()
        self.comp.blocks[block.id] = block
        return block
    def note(self, text, kind='note'):
        self.notes.append((text, kind))
        return self.say(text, kind)
    def paint(self): self.painted = True

u = _QueueUi()
u._echo('now')
now = _QueueWork()
assert u.start_turn(now)
test_eq([(b.body, b.tag) for b in u.comp.blocks.values()], [('now', 'user')])

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('second')
second = _QueueWork()
assert not u.start_turn(second)
test_eq([(b.body, b.tag) for b in u.comp.blocks.values()],
        [('queued · it runs when this turn ends · alt+up takes it back · ctrl+c stops this turn', 'note')])

u._echo('third')
third = _QueueWork()
assert not u.start_turn(third)
assert third.closed
assert all(b.body != 'third' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())
assert u._queued is second

u.turn = None
u._next_queued()
assert u.comp.started is second
assert u._queued is None
assert list(u.comp.blocks.values())[-1].body == 'second'

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('/clear me')
u._typed = '/clear me'                  # what Enter took from the composer
clear = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(clear)
assert u.take_back()
assert clear.closed and u._queued is None and u.buf.text == '/clear me', 'a queued command goes back as it was typed'
assert all(b.body != '/clear me' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('retry me')
retry = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(retry)
u.turn = None
def fail_spawn(work, name): raise RuntimeError('busy')
u.comp.spawn = fail_spawn
u._next_queued()
assert u._queued is retry
assert all(b.body != 'retry me' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())
assert u.notes[-1] == ('the waiting message did not start: RuntimeError: busy', 'error')


class _SteerAgent:
    def __init__(self, listening=True): self.listening, self.told, self.left = listening, [], []
    def steer(self, text):
        if self.listening: self.told.append(text)
        return 'told' if self.listening else ''
    def leftovers(self): out, self.left = self.left, []; return out

_QueueUi.steer = Ui.steer

u._echo('look at b')
assert u.steer('look at b')

test_eq([b.body for b in u.comp.blocks.values()], ['↪ look at b'])
test_eq(u._flash[0], 'sent · read after the current call')

assert not _QueueUi(None).steer('no turn of ours')
u = _QueueUi('running'); u.agent = _SteerAgent(listening=False)
assert not u.steer('nobody listening') and u.agent.told == []

u = _QueueUi('running'); u.agent = _SteerAgent()
held = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(held, prompt='queued line')
u.agent.left, u.turn = ['unread steer'], None
u._next_queued()
assert held.closed and u._queued is None
test_eq(u.comp.started.cr_frame.f_locals['prompt'], 'unread steer\n\nqueued line')

There are two ways to change the approval mode, one for each direction. tighten_approve, bound to ctrl+g, makes approvals one step stricter, from auto to edits to ask to off, and never looser, so pressing it by accident is harmless. cycle_approve, bound to shift+tab, goes round ask, edits and auto, then into plan mode. In plan mode every tool that acts on the world is withheld and the model proposes a plan instead. The next press leaves plan mode and goes back to ask. off is not on the cycle; from off, the next press goes to ask.

Python mode
Python mode gives the same prompt a second meaning. /python starts a Jupyter kernel that belongs to you, and from then on a line you type runs as Python in that kernel. /agent hands the line back to the model and leaves the kernel running; only /quit or the end of the process shuts it down. Everything else stays the same: the transcript, folding, approvals, attachments and slash commands. Only what enter does with the line changes.
The agent follows you into the kernel. enter_python points the agent’s Python tools at a Dhrishti overlay on the new kernel. An overlay is a layer over your namespace: the agent can read every name you defined and writes its own names into its layer, and it cannot rebind a name you made. The host stays the same object. enter_python then calls Agent.refresh, which drops the cached skills, registry and tools and gives the running model backend a fresh briefing with the new tools.
Related methods: run_code runs one cell you typed and prints its outputs as blocks, complete_python handles tab completion from the kernel, attach_session points the agent at someone else’s live Dhrishti session for --attach, and enable_agent_proxy makes this session’s agent callable from the Python prompt for --agent-proxy. /promote NAME copies one of the agent’s variables into your namespace.
pyrepl holds the parts that judge Python: the kernel, the overlay host, whether a line compiles, and how to colour it. It is imported only when Python mode starts, so a plain ramabana session needs no kernel. The tests that need a live kernel are on that page.

@implemented
class _Mem(MemHost, SessionHost):
    "A host recording what the agent runs, with the session tool group."
    def __init__(self, *a, **kw):
        super().__init__()
        self.ran, self.web, self.read_outside, self.kernel = [], False, False, None
    def run_python(self, code): self.ran.append(code); return '(ok)'
    def inspect_python(self, code, scope='isolated'): return '(ok)'
    def list_vars(self): return 'mem_var: int = 1'
    def restart_kernel(self): return 'restarted'
    def terminal_text(self, n=1): return ''

class _FakeKernel:
    base = 'http://127.0.0.1:65000'
    def __init__(self, cwd='.'): self.cwd = cwd
    async def start(self): return self

def _run_python(a): return next(t for t in a.tools if t.__name__ == 'run_python')
def _said(u, c): return u.transcript.block_text(list(c.blocks.values())[-1])

try: await swap_ui.enter_python()
finally: _pyrepl.Kernel = _realk

assert swap_agent.tools is not tools_before

PYREPL_MODULES = ('no_such_module',)
try: await swap_ui.enter_python()
finally: PYREPL_MODULES = ()

assert 'no_such_module' in _said(swap_ui, swap_comp) and 'ramabana[python]' in _said(swap_ui, swap_comp)

finally: _pyrepl.find_session = _realf

try: await swap_ui.enter_python()
finally: _pyrepl.Kernel = _realk

assert swap_ui.kernel is not None
assert any('left the attached session' in swap_ui.transcript.block_text(b)
           for b in swap_comp.blocks.values())

Shell lines
A line that starts with ! runs as a shell command in the first open folder, with no approval question, because you typed it yourself. run_shell_line runs it. Its output prints as one block, followed by the exit code, and a non-zero exit code prints as an error. The model never sees the command or its output.
So that the model knows this exists, main adds SHELL_NOTE to an interactive session’s extra_sp, the extra text appended to the agent’s briefing, before a resumed session builds its briefing. The note tells the model it can ask you to run a command with !. A one-turn run from the command line never gets the note. ! lines work only in agent mode; in Python mode the line is Python, and code_state rejects it because it does not compile.
The command runs in its own process group with stdin from /dev/null, so a command that tries to read from the terminal gets end of file instead of hanging. Ui.shell_proc holds the process while it runs, which is how ctrl+c reaches it (see stop further down).


source

Ui.run_shell_line
async def run_shell_line(
    command
):
Run one owner-typed ! line in the first open folder, printing its output and exit code.

sh_said

Replies are written in Markdown and drawn with Rich. MARKDOWN_THEME gives headings, inline code, links and lists their own colours in the active palette, instead of drawing everything in the terminal’s default colour. The text the model wrote is kept as plain Markdown; only the drawing adds colour. Rich markup inside a reply, such as [red], is shown as literal text, so a reply cannot inject terminal styling.
Ui.reply draws a reply. It uses Reply, Rich’s Markdown with code blocks drawn by ThemedCode, and compact_md, which joins plain paragraphs with single line breaks to save rows. fence_lang maps a code fence’s language to the highlighter’s name for it.
Here is the options row from the turn section in use. options_for decided that “refactor the runtime” earns a menu, ChoiceMenu.choose takes one keystroke at a time and returns (done, option), and Ui decides what the chosen option means for the prompt. Below, down moves the cursor and enter picks “plan”.

menu = ChoiceMenu(*options_for('refactor the runtime'))
test_eq(menu.choose('down'), (False, None))
test_eq(menu.choose('enter')[1].label, 'plan')
test_eq(ChoiceMenu('x', REFACTOR).choose('s')[1].label, 'scope')
test_eq(ChoiceMenu('x', REFACTOR).choose('escape'), (True, None))
test_eq(options_for('what does the runtime do?'), None)
print('\n'.join(r.plain for r in menu.render()))

                  code_theme='github-dark')

          if seg.style and seg.style.color and seg.style.color.triplet}

test_eq(inline.style.bgcolor, None)
test_eq(len(colors) >= 3, True)

The rest of the examples on this page build a complete surface in the notebook: an emulated terminal, a real compositor, and an agent from fake_agent whose model replies are scripted. Typing “refactor the runtime” and pressing enter opens the options row on screen.

tty.term.text().splitlines()[-1]

title: cli
text:
Folding
A block taller than FOLD (12 rows) starts folded, so a four-hundred-line result takes one row until you open it. ctrl+o opens all the working of the latest turn, every step and call, and a second press folds it again. alt+o does the same for every turn, and alt+1 to alt+9 open a single entry, newest first. The main screen leaves the mouse to the terminal, so selecting and copying work as in any scrollback. In the transcript view, a block opens and closes under the block cursor or with a click.

long = ui.say(Text('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(40))), 'tool')
long.collapsed, long.height


comp.toggle(long)
test_eq(long.collapsed, False)
comp.toggle(long)
long.collapsed

A one-line block has nothing to fold, so toggling it does nothing and raises no error.

short = ui.say(Text('one line'), 'tool')
comp.toggle(short), short.collapsed

A tool call folds to its own summary line rather than at FOLD rows, because the summary is what you want to read. A turn of thirty calls reads as thirty lines, and any one result is a keystroke away.
The fold is decided when the result arrives. A tool block is printed when the call starts, one hourglass row tall, and the result is put into the same block when the call returns. Teleprint’s print_block decides folding once, from the height at print time, which would be 1, so on its own it would leave every result open. _act therefore decides the fold again at the moment the result lands.

from ramabana.agent import Act


step = Act(tool='view_file', args={'path': 'runtime.py'}, summary='view runtime.py')
ui.on_act(step)
test_eq((ui.acts[step.id].height, ui.acts[step.id].collapsed), (1, False))

ui.on_act(step.finish('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(400))))
folded = ui.acts[step.id]
test_eq((folded.height, folded.collapsed), (401, True))
test_eq(len(comp._block_rows(folded)), 1)
assert step.summary in ui.transcript.block_text(folded)

comp.toggle(folded)
test_eq((folded.collapsed, len(comp._block_rows(folded))), (False, 401))
comp.toggle(folded)

The agent’s activity feed records each tool call as an Act. Text the model streams before a call is narration, so when a call starts, _close_seg closes that text as a step block above the call. The finished timeline stays on screen, and the reply block holds only the text after the last call.
While the reply is still arriving its block is tagged reply. /copy copies the final answer; the tool calls are the foldable trace above it.

tl_tty = EmuTty(72, 20)
tl_comp = Compositor(tl_tty)
tl_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await tl_comp.start()
tl_agent, _ = fake_agent()
tl_ui = Ui(tl_comp, tl_agent)
tl_acts = tl_agent.activity

seg = tl_ui.stream(None, 'Looking for it.\n\nTwo places, probably.\n')
call = tl_acts.start('search_code', {'query': 'threshold'})
tl_acts.finish(call, 'runtime.py:88\nagent.py:12')
seg = tl_ui.stream(seg, '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')
tl_ui.flush_stream()
tl_ui._seg_blk = None

timeline = list(tl_comp.blocks.values())
test_eq([b.tag for b in timeline], ['step', 'tool', 'reply'])
test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, True, False])
test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(timeline[0]), 'Looking for it.\n\nTwo places, probably.')
test_eq(len(tl_comp._block_rows(timeline[1])), 1)
test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(timeline[-1]), '''## Answer

Both of them.
''')

status_tty = EmuTty(72, 10)
status_comp = Compositor(status_tty)
status_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await status_comp.start()
status_agent, _ = fake_agent()
status_ui = Ui(status_comp, status_agent)
status_seg = status_ui.stream(None, 'Waiting for approval.\n')

test_eq(status_ui.transcript.block_text(status_blocks[-1]), 'Waiting for approval.\nDone.\n')

test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(answer), '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')
assert 'copied' in tl_ui.copy_last('reply')

test_eq(tl_ui.fold_work(), False)
test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, False, False])

test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, True, False])   # narration is not part of the working

_styles = {_md_line: None for _md_line in ()}

tl_ui._turn_at, tl_ui.turn = time.monotonic(), 'a turn'
footer = [r.plain for r in tl_ui.working()]

A delegation, where the agent hands a question to a sub-agent, shows as one entry with the sub-agent’s calls grouped under it. A sub-agent is a second agent the main one starts for a piece of work, here through delegate_search. It runs on the same recorded tool wrappers as its caller, so its calls arrive in the same Activity feed. Each of them carries a parent_action_id, which Agent sets from a per-thread stack of the delegate calls in flight, and Ui uses it to put the call under its parent. Without the grouping, the searches of three sub-agents would appear among the caller’s own calls.
A finished call folds to its summary, unless it is a write or a diff (see opens above). A failed call never folds, and nor does a running one, so folding never hides an error or progress. drillable lists the turn’s foldable calls, newest first, and drill(n) opens or folds the nth of them, which is what alt+1 to alt+9 do.

parent = tl_acts.start('delegate_search', {'question': 'who reads the threshold?'})
for q in ('threshold callers', 'reserve usage'):
    tl_acts.finish(tl_acts.start('search_code', {'query': q}, parent_action_id=parent.id), 'hits')
tl_acts.finish(parent, 'Three callers, all in runtime.py.')

group = tl_ui.acts[parent.id]
test_eq(len(tl_comp.blocks), 4)
test_eq((group.collapsed, len(tl_comp._block_rows(group))), (True, 1))
assert '2 calls' in tl_comp._ansi(tl_comp._block_rows(group)[0][1])
assert all(k.line() in tl_ui.transcript.block_text(group) for k in tl_ui.kids[parent.id])

failed = tl_acts.start('run_shell', {'command': 'pytest'})
tl_acts.finish(failed, 'FAILED test_reserve\nassert 0.9 <= 0.8', ok=False)
test_eq(tl_ui.acts[failed.id].collapsed, False)


test_eq([b.tag for b in tl_ui.drillable()], ['tool', 'tool', 'tool'])
test_eq(tl_ui.drill(2), True)
test_eq(group.collapsed, False)
test_eq(tl_ui.drill(2), True)
test_eq((group.collapsed, tl_ui.drill(99)), (True, False))

assert 'copied' in tl_ui.copy_last('turn')
test_eq(tl_ui._reply, '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')

test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, False)
assert 'mouse on' in tl_ui.set_mouse('on') and tl_ui.mouse
tl_ui.leave_transcript()
test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, True)
assert 'mouse off' in tl_ui.set_mouse('off')

title: cli
text:
Copying and browsing
There are two ways to copy out of the transcript, and both use the system clipboard. On the main screen the mouse belongs to the terminal, so you select and copy as in any scrollback. The transcript view, opened with ctrl+r or up, takes the mouse only while it is open (enter_transcript and leave_transcript). /copy and the view’s y key send the text over OSC 52, a terminal escape code for setting the clipboard, which works through ssh and tmux.
They copy a block’s source text rather than what is drawn: the Markdown the model wrote, or the arguments a tool got. Text taken off the screen would come back wrapped at the terminal’s width, indented by the gutter, and missing the code fences, so every block records its source when it is printed. transcript.block_text returns it, as the examples show.
The last three examples attach files: attach adds a picture once and refuses a duplicate, paste turns a pasted path into an attachment, and submit sends the attachments with the prompt and clears them.

md = 'Here is the fix.\n\n```python\nthreshold = 42\n```\n\nCall it from `runtime.py`.'
rblk = ui.stream(None, md[:20])
rblk = ui.stream(rblk, md[20:])
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(rblk), md)
rendered = '\n'.join(''.join(s.text for s in l) for l in comp._content_lines(rblk))
assert '```' not in rendered
assert '```python' in ui.transcript.block_text(rblk)


u = ui.say(Text('where is the threshold?'), 'user')
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(u), 'where is the threshold?')
wrapped = ui.say('x' * 200, 'note')
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(wrapped), 'x' * 200)
test_eq(wrapped.height > 1, True)
ui.copy_last('reply')


ui.enter_transcript()
test_eq((ui.transcript.active, ui.transcript.follow), (True, True))
ui.say(Text('search_code("threshold") landed while browsing'), 'tool')
assert 'landed while browsing' in tty.term.text()
sblk = ui.stream(None, 'and a reply streamed ')
sblk = ui.stream(sblk, 'in behind it')
ui.touch(now=True)
assert 'in behind it' in tty.term.text()
ui.transcript.move(-1)
test_eq(ui.transcript.follow, False)
ui.leave_transcript()
test_eq((ui.transcript.active, comp.paused), (False, False))


test_eq(ui.attach(shot), 'attached image shot.png (72B)')
test_eq(ui.attach(shot), 'shot.png is already attached')
ui.attach(snd_path)
test_eq([a.name for a in ui.attachments], ['shot.png', 'note.wav'])
assert 'shot.png' in ui.attach_row().plain and '/detach' in ui.attach_row().plain
test_eq(ui.detach('2'), 'dropped note.wav')
test_eq(ui.detach(), 'dropped 1 attachment')
test_eq(ui.detach(), 'nothing is attached')
test_eq(ui.attach(media_dir / 'gone.png'), 'cannot attach gone.png: no such file')
test_eq(ui.attach_row(), None)


ui.paste(str(shot))
test_eq([a.name for a in ui.attachments], ['shot.png'])
test_eq(ui.buf.text, '')
ui.paste('and this is ordinary text')
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'and this is ordinary text')
long_text = 'copied text ' * 100 + 'image.png'
ui.paste(long_text)
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'and this is ordinary text' + long_text)
ui.buf.clear()


ui.buf.insert('what is in this picture?')
await ui.submit()
test_eq(ui.attachments, [])

title: cli
text:
Approvals in a terminal
An approval is the question Ramabana asks before a tool with an effect runs: a file write, a shell command, a git commit and so on. The approval gate, Approvals, holds the model’s worker thread until a person answers. The request arrives on that thread and the answer comes from the event loop thread. While a question waits, the input line is where you answer it: y, n, a for the rest of the session, or n: followed by a reason.
Here a write is requested from another thread, the way a tool call does it:

tty2 = EmuTty(72, 12)
comp2 = Compositor(tty2)
comp2._register_signals = lambda: None
await comp2.start()
gated, _ = fake_agent(replies=['done'])
gated.approvals = Approvals(tools=WRITE_TOOLS, host=gated.host)
ui2 = Ui(comp2, gated)
comp2.on_key = ui2.on_key
ui2.paint()
threading.Thread(target=lambda: gated.approvals.request(
    'create_file', {'path': '/proj/notes.md', 'text': '# notes\n'}), daemon=True).start()
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
print(tty2.term.text())

The question block shows what you need to decide: the path, whether the write overwrites a file, and the start of what would be written. The input line now holds the approval question.

test_eq(ui2.ask.tool, 'create_file')
tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1]

parse_answer reads a typed answer. A line that is not an answer, such as a prompt typed at the wrong moment, does not count as a refusal. The question is shown again with a hint and keeps waiting. A waiting question also rings and shows itself again every REASK_EVERY seconds.

test_eq([parse_answer(t) for t in ('y', 'YES', 'n', 'no: too broad', 'n:', 'continue.', 'y: and add a test', 'approve', 'deny', 'ok')],
        [(True, ''), (True, ''), (False, ''), (False, 'too broad'), (False, ''), None, (True, 'and add a test'), (True, ''), (False, ''), None])

ui2.buf.insert('continue.')
ui2.on_key(Key('enter'))
assert ui2.ask is not None and ui2.ask.pending
assert 'not an answer' in tty2.term.text()
test_eq(ui2.buf.text, '')

rang = []
_write = tty2.write
tty2.write = lambda s: rang.append(s) if s == '\a' else _write(s)
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at -= BELL_IDLE + 1
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), True)
test_eq(rang, ['\a'])
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)

ui2.buf.insert('n: beca')
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at = time.monotonic()
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)
test_eq((ui2.buf.text, rang), ('n: beca', ['\a']))
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at -= BELL_IDLE + 1
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)
test_eq((ui2.buf.text, rang), ('n: beca', ['\a', '\a']))
ui2.buf.clear()
tty2.write = _write

The question takes the input line in any mode, including Python mode, where it is asked below. A reason is a sentence, and running it as Python would leave the gate unanswered.
y and a answer at once when nothing has been typed. n waits for enter, so that a reason can follow it: n and enter refuses, and n: put it in docs/ instead refuses with that reason, which gives the model something to act on instead of the word “denied”.

ui2.mode = 'python'
comp2.on_bytes(b'n: put it in docs/ instead')
tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1]


comp2.on_bytes(b'\r')
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
ui2.mode = 'agent'; ui2.paint()
ui2.ask, gated.approvals.history[-1].reply()

There are two histories, kept apart. The composer keeps your past prompts, and teleprint’s blocks are the history of the transcript. up and down recall a past prompt only when the cursor cannot move further inside a prompt of several lines. ctrl+r opens teleprint’s transcript view, where you can search old blocks, open them and copy them.

test_eq(bool(gated.approvals.history[-1]), False)
test_eq(tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1], '▌')
[b.tag for b in comp2.blocks.values()][-2:]

a approves the current request and sets the approval mode to auto for the rest of the session.

threading.Thread(target=lambda: gated.approvals.request('create_file', {'path': '/proj/b.md'}), daemon=True).start()
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
comp2.on_bytes(b'a')
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
gated.approvals.mode, gated.approvals.history[-1].note

title: cli
text:
Running it
mk_agent from ramabana.agent builds what the terminal runs. It makes a WorkspaceHost over the folders named on the command line, an Agent over that host, and an approval gate connected to both. A host is the object that supplies the agent’s tools and decides what they may touch: which folders, whether the network is reachable, and which writes need approval. mk_host builds the host alone. amain is the terminal loop that runs the Ui, and it stays short because the behaviour lives in Ui.
The prompt appears before the model is ready. begin builds the system prompt and tools and starts the model on a thread, and the status bar says starting model… meanwhile. A line sent before the model is up waits in the queue, like a line sent during a turn, and runs once the model is ready.
start_agent starts the turn model and then the code index, the search index behind search_code, so the index never delays the model. sync_index decides whether the index needs rebuilding: it rebuilds when a package or an open folder changed since the last good build, otherwise reopens the saved index, and logs which it did to <cfg>/kosha.log. warm_up runs start_agent off the loop with off_loop, and prints a note saying why when no model starts.


source

Ui.begin
def begin():
Start the model behind the prompt; lines sent meanwhile wait in the queue.




source

Ui.warm_up
async def warm_up():
Start the model off the loop; a start that fails says why in a note.




source

off_loop
async def off_loop(
    fn
):
fn() on a daemon thread, so quitting never waits for it.




source

start_agent
def start_agent(
    agent, closed:function=<lambda>, note:NoneType=None
):
Try the turn model, then start the code index search reads, whether the model came up or not; the backend, or None with agent.note saying why.




source

sync_index
def sync_index(
    host, cfg:NoneType=None, dirs:NoneType=None
):
Sync the code index when a package or root changed since the last good sync, else reopen it; run or skip, logged to <cfg>/kosha.log.


amain is the interactive loop: one terminal, one event loop, and one owner of the keyboard. It starts the compositor, connects keys, pastes, resizes and mouse events to the Ui, starts the model with begin, opens Python mode when asked, and on exit restores the terminal and shuts down the agent and any kernel.
Three helpers keep a broken terminal from breaking the session. AppTty is teleprint’s RealTty with one change: when the terminal hangs up, reading stops and writes are dropped, so the session quits instead of spinning. stderr_to sends Python’s stderr to a file while the screen belongs to the compositor, because a warning written straight to the terminal would scroll the transcript under the compositor’s frames; it also points faulthandler at that file so a hard crash leaves its stack trace there. stderr_log names the file, inside the session’s own run folder.
For --resume, pick_session lists the newest saved sessions from these folders and asks which to open, and show_resumed draws the last RESUME_SHOWN turns of the reopened session before the first prompt.


source

Without a terminal, ramabana runs one turn, which suits a pipe or a script. main is the entry point behind the ramabana command. It parses the options, builds the agent with mk_agent, and then either runs one turn with ask_once or starts the interactive session with amain. headless_prompt picks the one-turn prompt: the argument, or stdin when the argument is - or empty and stdin is a pipe. host_kw holds the host options the terminal adds. Outside tmux, an interactive session first starts itself again inside a tmux server of Ramabana’s own, as setup explains.

    agent, prompt, as_json:bool=False
):
Run one turn without a terminal and return the exit code.

The one-shot prompt: the argument, or stdin for - or an empty piped run.

main
def main(
    prompt:str='', # one turn and exit; omit for interactive
    root:str='.', # comma-separated folders: .,~/notes,/srv/app
    model:str=None, # turn model; omit for the routing default
    approve:str='ask', # ask | edits | auto | off | none (no gate)
    web:bool=True, # --no-web takes the web tools offline
    read_outside:bool=False, # reads reach any path; writes need --root
    subagent_writes:bool=True, # --no-subagent-writes restricts delegates to read-only tools
    vault:bool=False, # vishalakshi vault for reads; not in python mode
    pii:str='off', # off | redact | refuse PII from the vault
    pii_ner:bool=False, # --pii also gates titled names
    spec:bool=False, # enable OpenAPI, Azure and Google Discovery tools
    theme:str='auto', # auto | dark | light terminal palette
    max_tool_calls:str='auto', # auto | 20..400 tool calls per turn
    max_steps:str='auto', # auto | 8..80 model/tool-loop steps per turn
    cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', # config dir: skills, extensions, resumable history
    resume:str='', # saved session id/prefix, or 'latest'; bare --resume lists this folder's sessions to pick from
    all_folders:bool=False, # with a bare --resume, list sessions from every folder
    python:bool=False, # start in python mode, on a kernel of your own
    attach:str='', # join a live session; --kernels lists them
    agent_proxy:bool=False, # expose a restricted agent proxy in PyREPL
    kernels:bool=False, # list live sessions and exit
    json:bool=False, # with a prompt: print the full result as JSON
    bell:bool=True, # --no-bell silences turn-end and approval bells

    pane:str='auto', # auto | on | off: the `now` pane; auto in tmux

from fastcore.script import anno_parser

piped, _ = fake_agent(replies=['nothing changed since the last commit.'])

Ui.stop
def stop():
Escalate repeated Ctrl-C from cancellation to termination to exit.


stop is what ctrl+c does, and repeated presses escalate. During a turn, the first press cancels the turn’s run, the second terminates it, and the third quits; presses count as repeats only while they come within the agent’s cancel_grace seconds of each other. Each press also takes queued lines back into the composer, so nothing you typed is lost.
For a ! command, stop signals the command’s process group. The first ctrl+c sends SIGINT, and the next sends SIGKILL, however long after the first it comes. A command ended by a signal prints stopped, and the prompt is free once the process exits. Quitting kills a command that is still running.
on_key is patched once more so that ctrl+c stops a turn without clearing the composer, and alt+up pulls queued text back into the composer for editing.

import tempfile


armed = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'armed'
sh_ui.buf.insert(f"!trap '' INT; touch {armed}; sleep 30")
sh_ui.start_turn(sh_ui.submit())
sh_running = sh_ui.turn
for _ in range(100):   # SIGINT before the trap is set would end the shell, so wait until it is
    if armed.exists(): break
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
assert armed.exists()
sh_ui.stop()
await asyncio.sleep(0.6)   # longer than `cancel_grace`, and the command ignores SIGINT
test_eq(sh_running.done(), False)
sh_ui.stop()
await asyncio.wait_for(sh_running, 5)
sh_comp.stop()
test_eq((sh_ui.turn, sh_ui.shell_proc), (None, None))
sh_last = sh_ui.transcript.block_text(list(sh_comp.blocks.values())[-1])
assert 'stopped' in sh_last, [sh_ui.transcript.block_text(b) for b in list(sh_comp.blocks.values())[-4:]]
sh_last

Ui.on_key
def on_key(
    k
):
Ctrl-C stops without wiping the composer; alt+up pulls queued text back into it.



class _StopAgent:
    cancel_grace = 1
    def __init__(self):
        self.r = type('R', (), {'id': 'r1', 'terminal': False})()
    def run(self, run_id=''): return self.r
    def cancel(self, run_id): self.r.terminal = True; return {'state': 'detached'}
    def terminate(self, run_id): return {'state': 'terminated'}
    def leftovers(self): return []

class _StopUi:
    mark_read = Ui.mark_read
    def __init__(self):
        self.agent, self._stop_at, self._stop_count, self._stop_run = _StopAgent(), 0., 0, ''
        self.notes, self.turn, self.starting, self.shell_proc = [], None, False, None
        self._queued = None
        self._steered = []
    def note(self, text): self.notes.append(text)
    def take_back(self): return Ui.take_back(self)
    def paint(self): return None
    def _post(self, fn, *a): return fn(*a)

u = _StopUi()
Ui.stop(u); time.sleep(.02)
Ui.stop(u); time.sleep(.02)
test_eq(u.notes[:4], ['cancelling', 'detached', 'terminating', 'terminated'])
test_eq(Ui.stop(u), 'quit')

title: cli
text:
The now pane
The now pane is a small live view, in a tmux split beside the chat, of what the main agent and each sub-agent are doing at this moment: the turn, the call it is on, and each sub-agent run with its own calls. The surface writes a snapshot, now_snapshot, to <runs_dir>/now.json from its own loop: at most every PANE_EVERY seconds while calls change or a turn runs, and once more when the turn ends. ramabana-pane, from pane, reads that file and draws it.

/pane opens it with open_pane and /pane off closes it with close_pane.
--pane auto|on|off decides whether a session starts with it, through start_pane; auto opens it only inside tmux.
pane_cmd is the shell line that runs the viewer for a given file.

When the viewer crashes rather than quits, the surface reopens it, a limited number of times.


source

Ui.start_pane
def start_pane(
    mode:str='auto'
):
Open the first pane: on always tries, auto only in tmux with a runs dir.




source

Ui.close_pane
def close_pane():
Kill the now pane: what was closed, or ’’ when none was open.




source

Ui.open_pane
def open_pane(
    arg:str=''
):
/pane opens the now pane in a tmux split on the right; /pane off closes it.




source

pane_cmd
def pane_cmd(
    path
):
The shell line that draws the now pane for path.



import tempfile
from ramabana.pane import read_snapshot

class _Pane:
    def __init__(self, id): self.id, self.killed, self.dead = id, False, False
    def kill(self): self.killed = True
    def refresh(self): return self

class _Me:
    def __init__(self): self.splits = []
    def split(self, where, cmd, size=None): self.splits.append((where, cmd, size)); return _Pane('%9')

pane_tty = EmuTty(72, 14)
pane_comp = Compositor(pane_tty)
pane_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await pane_comp.start()
pane_ui = Ui(pane_comp, fake_agent(cfg=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()))[0])
now = pane_ui.agent.runs_dir/'now.json'
act = pane_ui.agent.activity.start('read_file', {'path': 'a.py'})
at = pane_ui._now_at
pane_ui.agent.activity.finish(act, 'ok')
test_eq(pane_ui._now_at, at)
assert read_snapshot(now)['root']['current'].startswith('read_file'), 'the write the call started made'
pane_ui.write_now(force=True)
assert pane_ui._now_at > at and read_snapshot(now)['root']['current'] == ''

me = pane_ui.agent.host.tmux_pane = _Me()
pane_ui.open_pane()
test_eq(me.splits, [('right', pane_cmd(now), '35%')])
pane_ui.open_pane()
test_eq(len(me.splits), 1)
test_eq(pane_ui.close_pane(), 'closed the pane %9')
assert pane_ui.pane is None
pane_tty.close()


from inspect import signature

assert 'graph' not in signature(mk_host).parameters
assert 'graph' not in signature(mk_agent).parameters
assert 'graph' not in signature(main).parameters


tl_ui.agent.activity.since()[-ACT_TAIL:]


tl_ui.turn = 'a turn'
footer = [r.plain for r in tl_ui.working()]
assert all(row[:8].count(':') != 2 for row in footer), footer
